rationale: Jesus names the figure: "he is the Elijah who was to come" (11:14, BSB). Malachi 4:5 promises that figure: "Behold, I will send you Elijah the prophet before the coming of the great and awesome Day of the LORD" (BSB); a script search of this app's Malachi finds Elijah's name only in that verse. Ellicott, Barnes, Poole and Gill on 11:14 all name Malachi 4:5. The type is explicit_reference, not quotation, because Jesus names Elijah and the expectation without quoting Malachi's words or using "it is written." The connection recurs inside Matthew at 17:10-13, where the disciples "understood that He was speaking to them about John the Baptist" (17:13, BSB). Graded explicit because the text names the figure Malachi promises. How this squares with John's own "I am not" (John 1:21, BSB) is a named disagreement reported in the lesson's Positions; it bears on the identification's sense, not on whether Matthew 11:14 points to Malachi.
